paragraphs: Hizhira tora (debarim kb, ch): "ki tibneh bayit chadash veasita maaqeh legaggeka velo tasim damim bebeteka ki yippol hannopel mimmennu". vezo hi mitzvat aseh min try"g mitzot shechayyab haadam laasot maaqeh legaggo v"g ditshammeshi haggag hu tashmish deaqray em habbayit shettachat haggag hu bet dira vetashmish qeba chayyab laasot maaqeh laggag abal em habbayit shettachat haggag eno bet dira ella hu bet otzerot ubet habbaqar vekayyotze dehu tashmish deaqray nimtza haggag hu aqray deaqray vahare zeh patur min hammaaqeh veayyen keneset haggedola choshen mishpat haggahat habbet yosep ot y" vechiqre leb choshen mishpat cheleq b siman tz" dap qs"d ammud b, ubesipre haqqadosh rab pealim katabti beinyan zeh bitshuba bs"d umihu im gag bet haotzar hu betzad beto ubime haqqayitz yeshenim al gag zeh shel bet haotzar chayyab bemaaqeh:

clarification.explanation: The Torah commands (Deuteronomy 22:8): "When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if anyone should fall from it" — this is a positive commandment among the 613, to make a parapet (railing) for a house's roof. This obligation applies when the house beneath the roof is a dwelling in regular use, even though use of the roof itself is only occasional. But if the house beneath the roof is a storeroom, a barn, and the like — whose own use is occasional — then the roof is "occasional upon occasional," and is therefore exempt from a parapet. Nevertheless, if the storeroom's roof is adjacent to the dwelling and people are accustomed to sleep on it in summer, it is obligated in a parapet like an ordinary roof.
takeaways: It is a Torah positive commandment to make a parapet for a dwelling's roof.
A storeroom/barn roof (occasional use upon occasional use) is exempt from a parapet.
If people sleep on the storeroom's roof in summer, it is obligated in a parapet.

paragraphs: Kol bayit sheen bo d' ammot al d' ammot patur gaggo min hammaaqeh mippene sheeno bet tashmish veeno rauy ledira veim ken habbayit atzmo have tashmish aqray vehaggag shello aqray deaqray ulehaki patur:

clarification.explanation: A house lacking the measure of four cubits by four cubits is exempt from a parapet, since such a small house is not fit for dwelling and is not considered a house of regular use. Since this is so, the use of the house itself is considered occasional, and consequently its roof is "occasional upon occasional" and exempt from a parapet.
takeaways: A house smaller than four by four cubits is not fit for dwelling and is therefore exempt from a parapet.

paragraphs: Bayit shel shuttapim chayyab bemaaqeh shenneemar ki yippol hannopel mimmennu lo tala hakkatub ella benopel ubatte kenesiyyot ubatte midrashot gaggotehem peturim mimmaaqeh mippene sheenam asuyim ledira:

clarification.explanation: A house with several partners is obligated in a parapet, since the verse ties the obligation to the very possibility that someone "might fall from it," not to who the owners are. But the roofs of synagogues and study halls are exempt from a parapet, since they were not built for dwelling.
takeaways: A jointly-owned house is obligated in a parapet — the obligation depends on the danger of falling, not on ownership.
Synagogue and study-hall roofs are exempt from a parapet, since they are not for dwelling.

paragraphs: Yishtaddel kol adam liqboa maaqeh shello beyado velo yaaseh "y shalicha ki mitzva bo yoter mibbishlucho (qiddushin m.) veqodem habberaka yomar leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinetteh veku' vihi noam veku' veaach"k yebarek "asher qiddeshanu bemitzotayv vetzivvanu laasot maaqeh" kemo shekkatab haramba"m za"l hilkot berakot pereq y":

clarification.explanation: It is proper for a person to install the parapet with his own hands, rather than appointing an agent to do it for him, since there is greater merit in a commandment performed by the person himself than by his agent. Before the blessing, one should say the formula "for the sake of the unification of the Holy One and His Divine Presence" and "Vihi Noam," and afterward bless: "who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to make a parapet."
takeaways: It is preferable to build the parapet oneself, not through an agent.
One says "for the sake of unification" and "Vihi Noam" before the blessing, then blesses "to make a parapet."

paragraphs: Gobah hammaaqeh en pachut measara tepachim kede shello yippol hannopel mimmennu vetzarik shettihyeh hammechitztza chazaqa kede sheyyishshaen adam aleha velo tippol sheim lo ken nimtza zeh oseh mikshol yoter linpila veyesh bene adam baabur noy veyippuy habbayit osim gobah hammaaqeh chamesh o shesh tepachim vetzarik lehazhiram shello yismeku al zeh ella yashlimu laasara:

clarification.explanation: The parapet's height must be at least ten handbreadths, so that a person leaning on it will not fall. It is also important that the partition be strong enough to lean on without collapsing — otherwise the parapet itself becomes an additional hazard for falling. Some people, out of aesthetic considerations, build a lower parapet, only five or six handbreadths — one should warn them not to settle for this, but to complete the height to ten handbreadths.
takeaways: The parapet's height must be at least ten handbreadths.
The parapet must be strong enough to lean on without collapsing.
One should not settle for a lower parapet for aesthetic reasons — always complete it to ten handbreadths.

paragraphs: Hammannicha gaggo belo maaqeh bittel mitzvat aseh veabar al lo taaseh diktib velo tasim damim bebeteka velav davqa gag ella kol maqom sheepshar likkashel bo velabo lide sakkana kegon sheyyesh lo bor bachatzero ben yesh bo mayim ben en bo mayim chayyab min hattora laasot lo mechitztza gabohha asara tepachim o yaaseh lo kesuy kede shello yippol adam sham veken kol mikshol sheyyesh bo sakkanat nepashot mitzvat aseh lahasiro ulehishshamer mimmennu shenneemar hishshamer leka ushemor napsheka veim lo hesir hammiksholot hammebiim lide sakkana bittel mitzvat aseh veabar al lo tasim damim bebetik vehannizhar alayv tabo birkat tob:

clarification.explanation: One who leaves his roof without a parapet thereby nullifies a positive commandment and also transgresses an explicit prohibition ("and you shall not bring bloodguilt on your house"). And this law is not limited to the roof alone — any place in the house or courtyard carrying a risk of stumbling and injury, such as a pit in the courtyard (whether it has water or not), must by Torah law be fenced with a ten-handbreadth partition or covered, so no one falls into it. Likewise any other hazard endangering life — it is a positive commandment to remove it and be careful of it, as it is said, "guard yourself and guard your soul." One who does not remove such hazards nullifies a positive commandment and transgresses "you shall not bring bloodguilt on your house," and one who is careful about this — a blessing of good will come upon him.
takeaways: The obligation to be careful of dangerous hazards applies to any dangerous spot in the house and courtyard, not only the roof.
A pit in the courtyard requires a ten-handbreadth fence or covering.
Neglecting a dangerous hazard nullifies a positive commandment and transgresses "you shall not bring bloodguilt on your house."

paragraphs: Poh irenu bagdad darkam laasot martep tachat qarqa hechatzer vegag hammartep hu atzmo hechatzer shehaggag asuy kippa shel abanim ubetok hakkippa ose challon patucha kede sheyyabo ora min hechatzer lammartep vesotemin hachallon bekissuy asuy beshappudin shel barzel mesoragin zeh bazeh shemmehem tikkanes haora lammartep vbsh"q rab pealim nishalti im tzarik lebarek kesheyyannicha zeh hakkissuy sheqqorin bearbe pngr" (soreg) vehaaleti deen lebarek ki hebeti sham dibre harab chayye adam kelal t"v seip k"d bekissuy beer shebbechatzer deen lebarek vekatab taam al zeh yeuyyan sham vaana abda amarti taam ki zo hassetima sheoseh laavir zeh shel hammartep happatucha beqarqa hechatzer hu tzarik lah belav haki kede sheyyelek veyaamod al gabbayv daapillu im lo haya bo omeq asara tepachim gam ken haya mukrach laasot zeh hakkissuy shel hpngr"h kede lidros sham velaken lo yebarek qb"v laasot maaqeh delav bishbil meaqeb bilbad hu oseh ella kede lehishtammesh "g hechalal g"k veod deepshar lomar dela mishtema leshon maaqeh al kissuy ella al mechitztza veek yebarek laasot maaqeh vei lanu lechaddesh lashon chadash bibrakot middatenu lekak yiqba zeh hakkissuy belo beraka:

clarification.explanation: In Baghdad it was customary to build a cellar beneath the courtyard, where the cellar's ceiling is actually the courtyard floor, made as a stone dome, with an open window inside it so light reaches the cellar from the courtyard — and the window is closed with a covering made of interlaced iron rods (called in Arabic "pangara"). The Ben Ish Chai was asked in his book "Rav Pe'alim" whether a blessing should be said when installing this covering, like the parapet blessing, and he ruled that no blessing should be said — similar to what "Chayei Adam" wrote regarding covering a well in a courtyard. The reason: this covering is needed anyway to allow walking over the cavity, even if it were not ten handbreadths deep, so the main purpose is not only preventing a fall but also using the area above the cavity. Furthermore, the term "parapet" belongs to a partition, not a covering, and one cannot invent a new blessing formula on one's own. Therefore this covering should be installed without a blessing.
takeaways: A cellar-window covering (like the "pangara" in Baghdad) does not require a "parapet" blessing.
The reason: the covering also serves for walking over the area, not only for preventing a fall, and is not linguistically a "parapet."
One should not invent a new blessing formula not established in halacha.

paragraphs: Harbeh debarim aseru chaza"l mishshum sakkana o shear hezzeq haggup unebaarem poh: tzarik lizzaher shello leekol basar vedag beyachad deqasheh letzaraat vetzarik lirchotz yadayv vegam piv ben basar ledag o lehepek veyokal pat sharuy benetayim vetob sheyyishteh mayim o shear mashqeh benetayim kede shello yiggeu yachad baitztomeka vekannizkar bishla"h vekol shekken detzarik shello lebashshelam o litzlotam yachad vaapillu besar op tzarik lizzaher bo kedin besar behema veayyen shiyyure beraka siman qy"v ot ch':

clarification.explanation: Our Sages forbade several things out of concern for danger or health harm, which will now be explained. One must be careful not to eat meat and fish together, since this is harmful and difficult for leprosy. One should wash hands and mouth between eating meat and fish (or vice versa), eat bread in between, and it is preferable to drink water or another beverage in between, so they do not meet each other in the stomach. All the more so, one should not cook or roast meat and fish together in the same pot. Fowl meat is included in this law, like domestic animal meat.
takeaways: Meat and fish should not be eaten together — including fowl meat.
One should wash hands and mouth, eat bread, and drink a beverage between eating meat and fish.
Meat and fish should not be cooked or roasted together.

paragraphs: Mayim veyayin vechalab udebash vetzir umureyas shennitgallu, asarum chaza"l shemma shata mehem nachash vehetil eres abal chometz veshemen ushear mashqin velo noda sheabar alehem nachash o remes sheyyesh bo eres hare ellu muttarim v"g demaran za"l katab en lachush bazeh zeman deen nechashim metzuyim benenu katebu haacharonim degam bazzeman hazzeh tzarik lizzaher veken katab haggaon chida" za"l denahagu beeretz yisrael lehishshamer bazeh velaken kol adam yazhir bene beto lekassot pi hakkaddim shel mayim bebeged veken hechabit mihu muttar bazeh hazzeman lirchotz bemayim megullin veayyen shiyyure beraka:

clarification.explanation: Water, wine, milk, honey, brine, and fish sauce that were "exposed" (left uncovered) — our Sages forbade them, out of concern a snake may have drunk from them and injected venom into them. But vinegar, oil, and other beverages with no concern a snake passed over them are permitted. Although Maran wrote that in our time there is no need for concern since snakes are not common, the later authorities wrote that even today one should be careful, and the Chida likewise wrote that in the Land of Israel the custom was to be careful about this — and therefore everyone should warn his household to cover the mouths of water jugs and barrels with cloth. Nevertheless, it is permitted in our time to wash with exposed water (not for drinking).
takeaways: Water, wine, milk, honey, brine, and fish sauce left exposed are forbidden for drinking, out of concern for snake venom; vinegar and oil are permitted.
Despite Maran's lenient view for our time, some are accustomed to be stringent and cover water and beverage containers.
It is permitted to wash with exposed water even today.

paragraphs: Veken tzarik lehizzaher meod bemayim mishshum met lishpok hammayim shehayu bayit shebbo met hammet vegam bayit sheni ubayit shelishi mikkol hatztzedadin shel habbayit shebbo hammet ukemo shekkatab haggaon chida" siman shl"t keminhag ir haqqodesh tvbb", veken hamminhag poh irenu bagdad vaapillu lirchotz bahem yadayim o lekabbes begadim asur veim shagu ubishshelu o apu beotam hammayim az hattabshil vehappat asur vetzarik lemakero legoy mihu bebayit shelishi en oserin happat vehattabshil vekol dabar sheyyesh bo hepsed kevan deikka mayim bebet hammet ken hamminhag poh irenu veayyen yerek abraham shehebio harab zekor leabraham za"l veim met beshabbat g"k neesarim hammayim kaamur udelo kayyesh mattirin vekannizkar bebirke yosep sham mihu im met beshabbat vehaya mayim bebet hammet ak mayim shel bayit sheni apu o bishshelu bo yesh lehattir abal mayim shel bet hammet oserin apillu im beshello o apu bo: veha dehammayim neesarin haynu davqa im hayu mayim lebaddam abal im beshaa shemmet hammet haya sharuy bammayim okelin en neesarin dekol midde deit beh peseda en malak hammavet oseh sham nezeq veyesh omerim apillu hammayim hayu chammin lebaddam biqdera al haesh en oseh bahem nezeq velaken en neesarim veen tzarik leshapekkam vekatab haggaon chida" za"l bebirke yosep sham shetztzarik lishpok gam im met yeled tok sheloshim yom deen mitabbelim alayv veken hamminhag poh irenu lishpok kol shennolad chay apillu chay shaa achat od katab harab za"l sham im meta shipcha goya bebet yisrael tzarik lishpok veim yisrael shekken lebet goy umet haggoy babbayit nistappeq harab za"l sham im tzarik yisrael hashshaken lishpok hammayim shebbebeto vekatab demistabbera leesor ayyen sham, mihu nireh, "g deyisrael hashshaken tzarik lishpok im kol zeh im yesh mayim bebet haggoy shebbo hammet veapu ubishshelu bebet yisrael hashshaken bemayim shellahem en leesor happat vehattabshil vekol midde deit beh hepsed, od katab harab za"l sham deim nitarebu mayim haasurim mishshum met bemayim kesherim la bateli beshishshim veneesru kol hammayim yeuyyan sham venireh li deim bishshelu o apu bahem yesh lehaqel: ubeinyan hattequpa tzarik lizzaher ak poh irenu bagdad usebiboteha en nizharim bazeh kelal vedarkenu lidrosh lahem ulehazhiram tamid sheyyannichu masmer barzel betok hechabit shel mayim ubetok hakkaddim tamid kol hashshana kullah deyesh lismok al zeh veshomer petaim Adonai:

clarification.explanation: One must be very careful with water that was in a house where a person died — to pour it out, and likewise water in the second and third houses adjacent on every side of the house of death, following the custom of Jerusalem and Baghdad. It is forbidden even to wash hands or launder clothes in it. If food or bread was mistakenly cooked or baked with this water — the dish or bread is forbidden, and should be sold to a gentile; but with water from the third house, the food is not forbidden, since there would be a loss involved. Even if the death occurred on the Sabbath, the water is still forbidden. Nevertheless, if at the time of death this water was already mixed into food (such as a cooked dish), it is not forbidden, since the Angel of Death does not cause harm where there would be a monetary loss; likewise hot water on the fire in a pot. Water should also be poured out in a house where an infant died within thirty days (for whom there is no mourning), and even if a gentile female servant died in a Jew's house. If a Jewish neighbor lives next to a gentile who died in his house, one should be stringent and pour out the neighbor's water too, but if food was cooked in the Jew's house with water from the gentile's house, the food should not be forbidden. This forbidden water, if mixed with kosher water, is not nullified in sixty and forbids the entire quantity — but if it was already cooked or baked with, one should be lenient. Regarding "tekufah water" (the transition times between seasons) — in Baghdad no care at all was customarily taken, but one should instruct and warn people to place an iron nail inside the water barrels and jugs all year round, and one may rely on this.
takeaways: Water in a house where someone died (and adjacent houses) should be poured out; forbidden to drink, wash, or launder with.
If mistakenly used in cooking, sell the food to a gentile, except water from the third house (due to loss).
Adding an iron nail to water vessels year-round is a substitute for the tekufah-water caution.

paragraphs: Im sakar bayit miyyisrael veqaba sham mezuzot lo yittelem kesheyyatza veim netalam qober et banayv vekannizkar baggemara (baba metzia qb.) veim sakar miggoy veqaba mezuzot im niknas acharayv yisrael lo yittelem veim niknas acharayv goy yittelem vekannizkar besiman rtz", od ameru baggemara bibrakot (nh.) mi shennotenim lo seper tora liqrot veeno qore, kos shel beraka veeno mebarek - meqatztzerim yamayv veyesh omerim ap haroeh nosein umolikin seper tora veeno omed mippanayv vekannizkar bechuppat eliyyahu raba shaar g' od ameru bipsachim (qy:) - lo yaabor adam al mayim shopekin yachep veim pizzeru alehem apar let lan bah vehallobesh minalayv beodam lachim beme harechitza qasheh leivvaron:

clarification.explanation: One who rented a house from a Jew and affixed mezuzot should not take them with him when leaving (there is a severe concern about this, as brought in the Gemara). If rented from a gentile and mezuzot were affixed — if a Jew moves in after him, he should not take them; if a gentile moves in after him, he should take them. Our Sages further said: one who is given the opportunity to read from the Torah scroll and does not read, or a cup of blessing and does not bless over it, shortens his days; and some say the same for one who sees people carrying a Torah scroll and does not stand before it. They also said: one should not walk barefoot over water spilled on the ground (unless dust was scattered over it), and one who puts on shoes while his feet are still wet from washing — this is harmful, leading to blindness.
takeaways: Do not remove a mezuzah you affixed in a house rented from a Jew upon leaving; from a gentile, it depends on who moves in after you.
One who refuses to read from the Torah or bless over a cup of blessing when given the opportunity shortens his days.
Do not walk barefoot over spilled water, and do not put on shoes with wet feet.

paragraphs: Od ameru sham bipsachim hattoleh sal upat betoko qasheh laaniyyut bar minnan upoh irenu haya hamminhag litlot pat haerub shel hair bebet hakkeneset, betok hakkis al haammud vaana abda tiqqanti liqboa teba qetanna petucha al haammud umannichin betokah haerub vekis haerub yotze venireh lekol vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam shello yitlu keakin shel lechem bechebel betok avir hattannur achar apiyyatam beod hattannur cham kede sheyyitztammequ umokere hallechem yimmatze bemaqom shemmokerin sham perurin harbeh ki hallechem shellanu darko lehitparer harbeh, vetzarik lehazhiram sheyyekabbedu haqqarqa achar gemar meker hallechem veyashliko betok hattannur veken yizzaharu baale battim babbattim bimqom akilatam ubimqom hatteba shemmunnach bah hallechem ki yimmatze perurin harbeh sham baqqarqa:

clarification.explanation: It is stated in the Gemara that one who hangs a basket with bread inside it invites poverty. In Baghdad it was customary to hang the eruv bread (enabling carrying on the Sabbath) in the synagogue, in a pouch on the reader's stand, but the Ben Ish Chai instituted instead fixing a small open box on the stand, so the eruv pouch protrudes and is visible to all, rather than truly "hanging." The public should be warned not to hang loaves of bread on a rope inside the oven opening after baking, while still hot, to dry them out — and likewise bread sellers must ensure they have a place for crumbs (since our bread crumbles a great deal), clean the ground after selling, and throw the crumbs into the oven. Homeowners too must keep the eating areas and bread storage places clean.
takeaways: Hanging a basket with bread invites poverty; one should ensure bread/eruv is not literally "hanging" in the air.
Loaves should not be hung on a rope in a hot oven opening to dry.
Cleanliness of bread crumbs must be maintained, both by sellers and at home.

paragraphs: Ameru baggemara deshabbat al yipsa adam pesia gassa deqasheh laenayim veita betamid pereq ' hammashheh neqabayv ba lide choli veken hu haddin behishtanna vegam ober mishshum bal teshaqqetzu veita baggemara deqiddushin (nt.) lo yimkor adam qarqa sheqqana rishona deeno siman tob gam lo tob leadam limkor nachalat abotayv ukemo sheamar nabot leachab (melakim k, g). od ameru baggemara deqamma (baba qamma tzg:) asur laqutz ilan sheoseh perot veim tzarik limqomo ayyen b"chayyim shaal" cheleq ' shehittir uleravcha demilleta yaaseh "y goy veayyen chatam soper. od ameru baggemara deqamma lo yimsor adam din al chabero lomar yishpot Adonai beni ubeneka heka deit leh dina beara. od ameru(berakot yt.) lo yiptach adam piv lassatan. od ameru (sanhedrin qd:) keshemmadkar ezeh tzara lachabero yomar lo lo alekem, shenneemar (eka , yb) lo alekem kol obere derek: veita baggemara dibrakot (dap k.) lehinnatzel meen hara habba pitom yomar ana mizzara deyosep qaatena ben porat yosep ben porat ale ayin (bereshit mt, kb). ubasseparim katub sheyyomar gam ken veyaaqob ish tam yosheb ohalim (bereshit kh, kz), gam yomar vaani berob chasdeka abo beteka eshtachaveh el hekal qadeshka beyirateka (tehillim h, ch). gam yomar vayyissa bilam et enayv vayyar et yisrael shoken lishbatayv vattehi alayv rucha elohim (bammidbar kd, b) vehaggaon chida" za"l katab minhag haolam lomar chamishsha velaken tolin etz metzuyyar bo tzurat kap sheyyesh bo chamishsha etzbaot vechaquq alayv ot Adonai vekatab beketer malkut demin haggemara mukach deanshe babel tzarik lehizzaher velishmor atzman min ayin hara tepe mishshear meqomot:

clarification.explanation:
Several practices and warnings the Ben Ish Chai brought from the words of our Sages: one should not take a large stride, which is harmful to the eyes; one who delays relieving himself (and likewise urination) comes to illness and transgresses "you shall not make yourselves detestable"; one should not sell land he acquired first (not a good sign), nor is it good to sell one's ancestral inheritance (like Naboth to Ahab); it is forbidden to cut down a fruit-bearing tree — and if its place is needed, some permitted it (Chaim Sha'al), and to be extra cautious, one should have it done through a gentile; one should not submit a grievance against his fellow to Heaven ("let God judge between me and you") when he has recourse to a court of law; one should not open his mouth to Satan; and when mentioning a misfortune to his fellow, he should say "not upon you" ("not upon you, all who pass by the way").

And to be saved from a sudden evil eye, one should say "I come from the seed of Joseph, a fruitful bough, Joseph, a fruitful bough by a well, whose branches run over the wall"; and in the books: also "and Jacob was a wholesome man, dwelling in tents," "and as for me, in the abundance of Your kindness, I will come into Your house...," and "and Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel..." The Chida wrote that the common custom is to say five (verses), and therefore people hang a hand-shaped figure with five fingers with the letter heh engraved on it. And in Keter Malchut: from the Gemara it is proven that the people of Babylon must be more careful of the evil eye than other places.
takeaways: Warnings: do not take a large stride (harmful to eyes); do not delay relieving oneself ("you shall not make yourselves detestable"); do not sell first-acquired land or ancestral inheritance; do not cut a fruit tree (if needed, through a gentile); do not open your mouth to Satan; say "not upon you" when mentioning misfortune.

To be saved from sudden evil eye: "I come from the seed of Joseph... a fruitful bough by a well" (and other verses); the custom is five verses, and a hand-shaped figure with the letter heh is hung; the people of Babylon must be especially careful of the evil eye.

paragraphs: Lo yitten tabshil veshum mashqeh tachat hammitta mippene sherucha raa shora alehen apillu im mekussim bikli barzel veyesh lizzaher apillu baokalin chayyin vaapillu bediabad asur leekol vekannizkar beshiyyure beraka udelo harab shebut yaaqob veyesh omerim shezzeh davqa tachat mitta sheyyeshenim aleha abal mitta sheyyoshebim aleha bishat akila en chashash veyesh mepaqpeqim bazeh veayyen shiyyure beraka kan ubemachaziq beraka orach chayyim siman rs"b, verauy lizzaher bekol gavna veyesh nizharin shello lehannicha maakol tachat hashshulchan ukemo shekkatab harab haggaon rabbi chayyim palagi'y za"l upoh irenu en nizharim bazeh umannichim tachat hashshulchan ubitshuba bsh"q rab pealim katabti bazeh veod yesh azharot mishshum rucha raa shello yachtzotz shinnayv beqoremit shel qaneh vaapillu min qaneh haggadel baagam mippene sheshshora alayv rucha raa veayyen tosepet shabbat siman v' veayyen shiyyure beraka ot yo"d yeuyyan sham veyesh lehistappeq baqqoremit shel qaneh achar sheasu oto machtzelet veken lo yokal shum ubatzal sheabar alehem layla achat achar shenniqlepu veim nishar meat miqqelippatam muttar vehaynu davqa im lebaddam abal im meorabim im shear okalim hen bebishshul hen bekibbush apillu qelupim legamre muttar veken amma debar vetzarik lehazhir anshe irenu beshumin habbaim mipperas shehem qelupim legamre:

clarification.explanation: One should not place a cooked dish or any beverage under the bed, since an evil spirit rests upon them — even if covered with an iron vessel, and even raw (uncooked) food. Even after the fact, it is forbidden to eat food that was under the bed. Some say the prohibition applies specifically to a bed one sleeps in, but a bed merely sat upon while eating carries no concern — though some disagree even about this, and it is therefore proper to be careful in every case. Some are also accustomed not to place food under the table, although in Baghdad this was not strictly observed. Another matter of an evil spirit: one should not pick teeth with a reed splinter (even a reed grown in a marsh), since an evil spirit rests upon it — and there is doubt whether this law applies even after the reed has been made into a mat. Likewise one should not eat garlic and onion left overnight after peeling, unless a bit of peel remains on them; but if they are mixed with other foods (in cooking or pickling), it is permitted even if fully peeled — and so is the common practice. One should be especially warned regarding garlic brought from Persia, which arrives already fully peeled.
takeaways: It is forbidden to place a cooked dish, beverage, or food under the bed, due to an evil spirit — even covered, even after the fact.
One should not pick teeth with a reed splinter, and should not eat peeled garlic/onion left alone overnight.
Garlic and onion mixed with other foods are permitted even fully peeled.

paragraphs: Tzarik lizzaher shello yabo lepiv mizzeat haadam shehi kemo sam hammavet chutz mizzeat happanim deenah mazzeqet veasu siman laddabar bezeat appeka tokal lechem (bereshit g, yt) ulekak yizzaher shello yimtzotz o yaloq bilshono bibsaro o bibsar adam acher chutz min happanim shemma yehe sham zea veyazziq lo veken lo yannicha peri o shum dabar maakol ben chaluqo libsaro veyizzaher shello yitten maot betok piv velo yitten pas yado tachat shechyo veayyen shulchan gabohha siman qy"v seip qatan y"g vy"d:

clarification.explanation: One must be careful that another person's sweat not reach one's mouth, since it is like a deadly poison — except for facial sweat, which is not harmful (hinted at in the verse "by the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread"). Therefore one should not suck or lick with the tongue one's own flesh or another person's, except the face, out of concern for harmful sweat. Likewise, one should not place fruit or any food between clothing and the body, should not put coins in the mouth, and should not place a hand beneath the armpit — all out of concern for harmful sweat.
takeaways: Another person's sweat (besides facial sweat) is harmful like poison — avoid sucking or licking human flesh.
Do not place food between clothing and the body, coins in the mouth, or a hand beneath the armpit.

paragraphs: Ita biktubbot dap s" (ammud ) im raa maakol venitavva lo venizdammen lo al yede kak roq bepiv lo yibla haroq ella yaplitennu ki yazziq lo veita beshabbat dap "h im hiqqiz dam yishpok haddam tekep bachapira shebbaqqarqa hechatzer mippene sheim yishteh chatul middam zeh qasheh lechulsha veken yesh lizzaher keshemmotzi dam "y aluqa o im yatza dam mechatemo veita baggemara dechullin lo yesheb adam tachat hammarzeb hayyotze min haggag veita baggemara deyoma lo yashan beminalim veod ita sham dap p"d im okel adam pat chittin chamma qasheh lecholi haqqaddachat veken ameru birushalmi pat chamma chammatah betziddah venireh deayyeri bachamma yoter midday deken mashma leshon chammime dachamime veken yesh lehokicha miggemara dechullin dap q"h ammud ' mihu beir haqqodesh yerushalayim chosheshin bistam pat chamma apillu sheenah chamma yoter midday:

clarification.explanation: If one saw food and craved it, and as a result saliva formed in his mouth — he should not swallow the saliva but spit it out, since this is harmful. After bloodletting, the blood should be poured immediately into a hole dug in the courtyard ground, so a cat does not drink from it (which causes weakness); the same care applies to blood from a leech or blood from the nose. One should not sit beneath a roof gutter (drainpipe). One should not sleep in shoes. Eating overly hot wheat bread is harmful for fever (high heat) — this refers to bread that is too hot, not ordinary bread; but in Jerusalem the custom was to be careful of all hot bread, even if not especially hot.
takeaways: Saliva formed from craving food should be spat out, not swallowed.
Blood from bloodletting, a leech, or the nose should be poured immediately into a hole, not left exposed.
Do not sit under a roof gutter, do not sleep in shoes, and be careful of overly hot wheat bread.

paragraphs: Lo yokal mimmah sheakal akbar umimmah sheakal chatul velo yokal leb behema velo yihyeh ragil bezetim velo yishteh mayim shel shiyyure rechitza velo yirchotz raglayv zo al gab zo velo yannicha kelayv tachat meraashotayv dekol ellu hem qashim leshikcha, lo yaabor ben shene gemallim o ben shette nashim o ben shene kelabim vehaynu davqa im mekavvenim yachad vedavqa im holek lebaddo abal im yesh adam acher holek betziddo beshaveh let lan bah venireh li deim hakkeleb echad yosheb al haitztabba vehashsheni baqqarqa lematta deshetach haitztabba gabohha miggab hakkeleb let lan bah veken hu haddin bishte nashim vekol ellu hannizkarim im yesh ben zeh lazeh d' ammot let lan bah vekatub betzavvaot rabbenu yehuda hechasid za"l lo yittotz tannur vekirayim sheopin bo kede lehishtammesh beoto maqom velo yistom challon o petach legamre ella yannicha chor kol shehu veen mekassin tzoa beeper cham velo yoshib bebeto tarnegolet al betzim legaddel eprochim:

clarification.explanation: One should not eat from what a mouse or cat has eaten, should not eat an animal's heart, should not habitually eat olives, should not drink leftover washing water, should not wash one foot over the other, and should not place clothes under a pillow — all of these are harmful to memory. One should not pass between two camels, two women, or two dogs positioned facing each other while walking alone; but if someone else walks alongside him, there is no concern. Likewise, if one dog sits on a bench higher than the other dog's back on the ground, there is no concern, and the same law applies to two women. Likewise, if there is a distance of four cubits between the two, there is no concern. In the testament of Rabbeinu Yehuda HeChasid: one should not demolish an oven or stove to reuse its place, should not seal a window or doorway completely (a small hole should be left), should not cover excrement with hot ash, and should not seat a hen in the house to brood on eggs.
takeaways: Things causing forgetfulness: eating what a mouse/cat touched, an animal's heart, excessive olives, washing water, and one foot over the other.
Do not pass between two camels/women/dogs facing each other while walking alone — unless accompanied, or there is distance/height difference.
The testament of Rabbi Yehuda HeChasid: do not seal an opening completely, do not cover excrement with hot ash, do not demolish an oven for reuse in its place.

paragraphs: Katub beshaar rucha haqqodesh lerabbenu haari"y za"l lo yistakkel baharugim o tzelubim veyitracheq veyibrach min recha nebela o shear recha ra ki yazziq lannepesh velo yilbash shene malbushim zeh betok zeh beyachad deqasheh leshikcha velo yishlob etzbaot yadayv zo al zo hayyamin bismol velo yikbeh hanner bepiv vetob lipshot zerootayv tamid letzad panim shello yihyu zerootayv laachorayv vetob lo bazeh:

clarification.explanation: According to the secret of the holy spirit of the Arizal: one should not look at the executed or the hanged, and should keep away and flee from the smell of a carcass or another bad smell, since this harms the soul. One should not wear two garments one inside the other at once, since this is harmful to memory. One should not interlace the fingers of one hand over the other (the right hand over the left). One should not extinguish a candle with the mouth. And it is always good to extend the arms forward and not hold them behind the body.
takeaways: According to the Arizal's secret: keep away from the sight of the executed/hanged and from bad smells, since this harms the soul.
Do not wear two garments one inside the other, and do not interlace the right hand's fingers with the left's — harmful to memory.
Do not extinguish a candle with the mouth; it is good to extend the arms forward, not hold them behind the body.
